# Jordan — Emotional Thread

Right now Jordan is in a holding pattern that doesn't feel like one anymore. The reorg finally landed on September 1st — not a layoff, but a transfer to "legacy marketing," the place people get parked, under a new manager named Priya starting September 21st. A week later that news barely registers as bad. There's an onsite interview at Northlight on September 24th, three days after Priya starts managing him, and Jordan is aware of how cringey that timing is and doing it anyway.

The throughline of the last two months is a pattern Jordan has named explicitly and keeps watching happen anyway: something at work lands wrong — Marcus's whiplash feedback, a dismissed demo, the reorg itself — and Jordan withdraws. Blinds down, phone off, no food, no texts. It happened hard on August 3rd, again on the 11th, again on the 24th. Each time the way out was the same: eventually get to Groundwork and build something on Coda, the music-practice app that's been going for months, or have Mika show up uninvited with food and no questions. By September 1st, the withdrawal after the reorg news lasted twenty minutes instead of a full day — the first time Jordan noted the "middle part" actually getting shorter, something written off as impossible in earlier entries.

The bigger shift has been about hiding things versus handing them over. Jordan ran a five-week blackout on Mom about the whole restructuring, only breaking it during her Labor Day visit, and she named it plainly: "I wish you'd told me in July." A near-identical move happened with Dev after a cancelled lunch became an honest text on August 27th about shutting down rather than being "busy" — Dev's response ("I disappear too, I just do it with a bass in my hands") opened something. Lena, before leaving Meridian on August 28th, caught Jordan reflexively saying "I don't think I'd have good enough experience" for a referral and called it out on the spot. That same self-doubt reflex showed up again on September 16th with Mika's open-mic link, and this time Jordan caught it mid-thought and signed up anyway.

Coda itself became more than a coping mechanism — first a place to go feel competent on bad nights, then, through Dev using it on September 3rd, a real design lesson: Jordan had built a feature that collected evidence of being okay, not a tool that worked for someone practicing toward an actual deadline. That realization got rebuilt into the app on September 15th and, by September 17th, into the spine of the portfolio case study for Northlight — a story that took months of journal entries to actually see the shape of.

Threads still open: the Northlight onsite on the 24th and whether an offer arrives before or after things settle with Priya. The open mic at the Fern on September 27th, already signed up for. Dev's gig on the 19th, which Jordan will be at. The recurring dream about the empty office — third time now, but the first time Jordan found the stairs. And underneath all of it, the line from September 14th still sitting there unresolved: the wanting-to-disappear feeling is still true when it hits, "it's just no longer the last word."
